objective: Add a private, allowlist-gated GitHub-OAuth admin surface for the F007 adviser/download subsystem, proving F007 acceptance step 3 (ONLY an allowlisted GitHub admin can use admin functions) and step 4 (negative-security + audit scenarios). The standard GitHub OAuth web flow (authorize redirect -> callback -> exchange code for token -> fetch the GitHub login) is CSRF-protected with a signed, cookie-bound `state`. Only a GitHub login in the configured allowlist (default `stsyg`) becomes admin; a successful GitHub auth for a NON-allowlisted user is rejected (no session issued) and audited. On allowlisted login a STATELESS signed session cookie (stdlib HMAC over login|issued|expiry, HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite, constant-time verified, expiry-enforced) is issued and re-verified on every admin request - tamper/forgery/expiry -> 401. State-changing admin actions additionally require a signed per-session CSRF token verified server-side. Four admin functions sit behind the guard: the AI kill switch (toggling the EXISTING S2 abuse_flag), a review/contradiction queue (READ + approve/reject/defer over the existing review_item table), a READ-ONLY source-health view (over the existing source/scan_run/snapshot tables), and a READ/VALIDATE-ONLY YAML config-diff (validate a candidate via the existing config loader + diff vs the running config; never writes config). Every auth attempt (success + denied) and every mutating action (and every protected-endpoint denial) is appended to admin_audit via migration 0009 - with actor, action, outcome, reason, and non-secret context (never a token, secret, cookie, or raw OAuth code). NO admin_session table; NO new runtime dependency; NO Redis; no real github.com network in tests/smoke.

acceptance_criteria: 1. GitHub OAuth login: GET /admin/login sets a signed, cookie-bound `state` and redirects to the configured GitHub authorize URL; GET /admin/callback verifies `state` (query matches cookie AND signature/TTL valid), exchanges the code for a token, and fetches the GitHub login. Client id/secret come from config/env, never hardcoded, never logged. Any failure denies. The real UrllibGitHubOAuthClient is wired; tests/smoke use a DI fake and never contact github.com.

2. Allowlist: only a GitHub login in the configured allowlist (default `stsyg`) becomes admin. A successful GitHub auth for a NON-allowlisted user is REJECTED (403, no session cookie) and audited as a denied attempt (actor=login, action=login, outcome=denied, reason=not_allowlisted).

3. Stateless signed session cookie (Q6): after allowlisted login an HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite signed cookie carrying login|issued|expiry is issued (stdlib HMAC); every admin request re-verifies signature (constant-time) + expiry; a missing cookie -> 401 (unauthenticated), a tampered/forged/expired cookie -> 401 (invalid_cookie). NO session table.

4. CSRF protection: state-changing admin actions (kill-switch toggle, review-queue action, config-diff) require a signed per-session CSRF token (GET /admin/session issues it) verified server-side (constant-time); missing/invalid -> 403 (invalid_csrf) and audited. The OAuth `state` separately covers the login flow.

5a. AI kill-switch toggle: POST /admin/kill-switch toggles the EXISTING S2 abuse_flag (name ai_kill_switch) via the existing abuse store; GET /admin/kill-switch reports persisted + env-override + effective. The toggle is audited.

5b. Review/contradiction queue: GET /admin/review-queue lists items from the existing review_item table (no fabricated data; empty when none); POST /admin/review-queue/{id}/action advances admin_disposition to approved/rejected/deferred (audited); invalid disposition -> 422 (audited), unknown id -> 404 (audited).
5c. Source-health view: GET /admin/source-health is READ-ONLY over the existing source/scan_run/snapshot tables (last scan status/finished_at, error count, last snapshot fetch); no new data.

5d. Config-diff view: POST /admin/config-diff validates a candidate YAML via the EXISTING config loader and returns a unified diff vs the running/committed config plus validity + problems; it NEVER writes config.

6. PostgreSQL audit log (migration 0009): every auth attempt (success + denied) and every mutating action (and every protected-endpoint denial) is appended to admin_audit with actor (GitHub login or null pre-identity), action, outcome, reason, non-secret context, and created_at. NO token/secret/cookie/raw-code ever appears in an audit row (secret-stripping enforced).

7. Migration 0009 (down_revision 0008_adviser_abuse_controls) creates the admin_audit table, provides upgrade() + downgrade(), and round-trips clean (up -> down -> up, no drift). Revisions stay linear (0008 -> 0009).

8. No new runtime dependency and no Redis (FastAPI + Python stdlib only); no admin_session table; no real github.com network in tests/smoke; existing SSRF/reject_urls guards intact; no LLM-to-publication path; no secrets in source/logs/tests/examples; containers keep health checks; amd64/arm64 preserved.

9. Negative-security matrix (tested + live): non-allowlisted user denied+audited; forged/expired/tampered cookie denied (401)+audited; missing/invalid CSRF denied (403)+audited; missing/mismatched/invalid OAuth state denied (401)+audited; missing code denied (400)+audited; unauthenticated access to EVERY admin function denied (401)+audited.

risks.data_migration: Migration 0009 (down_revision 0008_adviser_abuse_controls) adds the single admin_audit table and round-trips clean (up -> down -> up, no drift; proven live). Revisions stay linear (0008 -> 0009). No backfill, no destructive change to existing tables. Review-queue decisions reuse the existing review_item.admin_disposition column (no new queue table).
risks.security_privacy: Admin is gated by GitHub OAuth + a config allowlist (default `stsyg`); a non-allowlisted GitHub auth is rejected and audited. The session is a STATELESS stdlib-HMAC signed cookie (HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite, constant-time verify, expiry-enforced) - no admin_session table, no JWT lib. Login is CSRF-protected by a signed cookie-bound OAuth `state`; mutations require a signed per-session CSRF token. The OAuth client id/secret + cookie signing key come from env only (never hardcoded/logged); the access token and raw OAuth code are never logged, audited, or returned. admin_audit strips any secret-looking context key (secret/token/password/cookie/code/authorization/...); a live scan of the audit rows found zero leaked secrets. Real github.com is never networked in tests/smoke (DI fake). Public endpoints keep the reject_urls/SSRF guard.
risks.portability: No new runtime dependency and no Redis (Q9): FastAPI + Python stdlib (hmac, hashlib, secrets, urllib, difflib) + the already-present SQLAlchemy/Alembic + the existing config loader only. amd64/arm64 unaffected; containers keep health checks. The audit log lives in PostgreSQL; no extra service. The real OAuth URLs are configurable (GitHub Enterprise/self-hosted friendly) with no code backdoor.
risks.zero_cost_safety: The admin surface neither re-derives Z0/quota/classification nor creates any LLM-to-publication path. The kill-switch toggle reuses the existing S2 abuse mechanism; config-diff is READ/VALIDATE only and never writes config; the review-queue action only advances an existing review_item disposition.
risks.immutability: admin_audit is additive and orthogonal to the domain catalogue; existing immutability/separation triggers are untouched. Store writes use their own engine.begin() transactions independent of the read-only request session. Audit rows are append-only in spirit (insert-only path).
risks.regression: Additive: a new admin/ package + 1 ORM model + migration 0009 + settings knobs + main.py router include + a web /admin surface + additive compose/env + additive tests. The deterministic adviser core and S1/S2/S3 behaviour are unchanged (the domain-table-count test was widened by exactly the one new admin_audit table, not weakened).
risks.supply_chain: No new npm or Python dependency; requirements-sync + npm audit (--omit=dev, 0 vulns) + pip-audit + detect-secrets stay green.
